title: The Uhlenbeck-Ford model in two dimensions: Reference system for fluid-phase free-energy calculations
authors: Samuel Cajahuaringa, Rodolfo Paula Leite, Maurice de Koning
abstract: We investigate the Uhlenbeck-Ford (UF) model as a reference system for free-energy calculations in two-dimensional (2D) fluids. The 2D virial coefficients are computed exactly up to tenth order and combined with molecular simulation data to construct highly accurate numerical representations of the equation of state and the excess Helmholtz free energy. We then determine the phase diagram of the model in order to establish the thermodynamic stability limits of the fluid phase and thereby identify the range of applicability of the UF model as a fluid reference system. In the course of this analysis, we identify the solid, hexatic, and fluid phases, and show that the fluid remains the only thermodynamically stable phase, independent of density, for scaling parameters up to $p\lesssim 70$. Finally, we demonstrate the practical applicability of the 2D UF model as a reference system through thermodynamic integration calculations of the free energy of a two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid.
summary: This paper establishes the 2D Uhlenbeck-Ford model as a robust and highly accurate reference fluid for calculating the thermodynamic properties of other two-dimensional fluids. By combining exact virial expansions with advanced free-energy techniques like Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Integration, the authors validate its use across various physical regimes.
main_problem: The study investigates using the Uhlenbeck-Ford (UF) model as a highly accurate reference system for calculating the free energy of two-dimensional (2D) fluids.
main_result: The 2D UF model was shown to be an excellent reference fluid, accurately predicting thermodynamic properties and remaining thermodynamically stable in the fluid phase up to significant scaling parameters ($p \lesssim 70$).
method: The authors employed advanced statistical mechanics techniques including exact computation of virial coefficients (up to tenth order) and Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Integration (NETI).
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the 2D Uhlenbeck-Ford (UF) model, characterized by a specific pair potential. The methodology involves constructing an equation of state and excess Helmholtz free energy using this reference fluid.
key_observables: Equation of State (EOS), excess Helmholtz free energy ($ eta F_{exc}$), phase diagram boundaries, reduced pressure ($ eta b P$), and structural order parameters ($\Psi_6$).
important_parameters: Dimensionless density variable ($x$) and the scaling parameter $p$, which dictates stability limits.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve truncating the virial expansion (up to 10th order) and using NETI, whose errors are related to finite switching times.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares reduced pressure vs. dimensionless variable $x$ for the 2D UF model, contrasting exact virial expansions with Molecular Dynamics simulation data.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the accuracy of the UF model via high-order virial coefficient calculations and comparison to MD simulations. It then uses this reference system in thermodynamic integration methods (NETI) to calculate the free energy of a target fluid, validating its applicability against other theoretical models.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the rigorous application of advanced statistical mechanics techniques like NETI for free-energy calculations provides methodological insights applicable to determining equilibrium properties in complex quantum many-body systems where direct simulation is hard.

FIG. 5. Phase diagram of the two-dimensional UF model. The solid blue and red lines depict the boundaries between the solid and hex- atic and between the hexatic and fluid phases, respectively. These were obtained by visually identifying the temperatures at which ΨT and Ψ6, respectively, undergo their rapid decrease, corroborated by the evolution of the static structure factor S(k). The shaded blue re- gion indicates the hexatic phase. The horizontal black dashed line corresponds to the scaling parameter p = 70 level. The inset shows an enlarged view of the hexatic phase region.
